generator.params.basal_area.note: The leaf area its `basal` look draws on an organ 1 m long (visual forms Skill 1, 2026-10-14; plantc atlas), so it shades with what it shows: the look now takes its card from the taxa's characters, where before it drew the generic card (0.235).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960), as Anaphalis margaritacea: stems 20 cm to 80 cm tall. The typical value is the one the plant was drawn at before, inside the source's range.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960), as Anaphalis margaritacea: leaves 2 mm to 2 cm wide.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a woolly, grey-green herb of leafy stems topped by flat clusters of papery white flower heads. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 0.6 m tall at 4 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: grey-green woolly leaves; white heads with yellow centres.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.inflorescence.note: Gleason and Cronquist's account of the species, as quoted in search results (the page itself was not read): heads 1 cm wide or less, numerous and crowded in a short, broad inflorescence; field guides call the array flat-topped to rounded. Read as a corymb, its heads reaching about one level.

appearance.organs.flower.note: Its array drawn head by head (spec rework L1c): its kind from its characters, by the rule at the flowering plants; about 40 heads, by eye (floras say only that they are numerous), each about 9 mm across (involucres 6 to 8, to 10 mm wide, in the Flora of North America), its pearly white phyllaries drawn as phyllaries (spec rework P2): about 40 in 5 rows, by eye, their upper halves turned 60 degrees outward round the yellowish florets as the heads open in photographs, the disc half the head's width. From floras and extension pages as quoted in search results; the pages themselves were not read.

traits.involucre_diameter_m.note: FNA's account of the species (Nesom, volume 19), as search results quote copies of its text (the pages themselves were not read): involucres 5 to 7 mm tall and 6 to 8 mm across, rarely 10; phyllaries ovate to nearly linear, their tips white and opaque.

traits.involucre_height_m.note: FNA's account of the species (Nesom, volume 19), as search results quote copies of its text (the pages themselves were not read): involucres 5 to 7 mm tall and 6 to 8 mm across, rarely 10.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Anaphalis margaritacea (p. 485): leaves 5-15 cm long, 2-20 mm wide.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, A. margaritacea (p. 485): leaves linear to lance-linear, the lowest oblanceolate.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, A. margaritacea (p. 485): leaves sessile and more or less clasping.

traits.flowering_months.note: FNA's account of the species, as search results quote copies of it (the page itself was not read): flowering July to October, sporadically longer. Abrams' months are lost in the scan's OCR.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: FNA's account of the species, as search results quote copies of it (the page itself was not read): cypselae 0.5-1 mm. Abrams (p. 485): achenes small, oblong-obovoid.

traits.height_max_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L2922417), as no source read gives it.

traits.leaf_apex.note: Flora of China, Anaphalis margaritacea (read 2026-10-18): the middle stem leaves taper to a long point with a small tip; the lower leaves, withered by flowering, are obtuse.
